# C1 — Redundant Computation

*Level 1 card. 8 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged. This includes code whose results are never consumed (dead code, resultless computation), operations that repeat work already done in the same scope (repeated computation, redundant assignments), setup and initialization on paths where results are unused (unnecessary initialization), excessive invocation of runtime housekeeping (GC calls, unchecked logging), and intermediate variables that add overhead without improving clarity. The common thread is that removing or simplifying these operations would not change program behavior but would reduce energy consumption.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | delete the assignment or the unreachable statement | yes, scales with input |
| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | remove the assignment that leaves state unchanged | **no — advisory only** |
| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | remove the control-flow construct that has no effect | **no — advisory only** |
| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | compute once into a local and reuse it | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | delete the computation whose product is never consumed | yes, scales with input |
| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | move the initialisation inside the branch that needs it | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | inline the single-use intermediate | **no — advisory only** |
| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | drop the manual collection, or guard the expensive log argument | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C1.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S6.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S7.md`, `reference/root-causes/C1.S8.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C1.S4 vs C3.S2 Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values** — C1.S4 is repetition across sequential statements in straight-line code. C3.S2 is repetition across loop iterations.  If hoisting means "move it above the `for`", it is C3.S2.
- **C1.S4 vs C8.S1 Missing Memoization Cache** — C1.S4 stays inside one invocation.  C8.S1 spans separate invocations and its repair is a cache that outlives the call.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
